pr_title: Fix a regression in formatting caused by the 'FirstOrDefault' primitive added in 7.0.0-Preview1
pr_body:
<!-- Anything that looks like this is a comment and can't be seen after the Pull Request is created. -->

# PR Summary

Fix #10554

Hidden members should not be returned by any fuzzy searches, such as searching by 'match' or enumerating the collection. They are returned only if the member names are explicitly looked for. `FirstOrDefault` is a fuzzy search, so it should ignore the hidden members.

issue_context.title: Write-Output of class with hidden params regression in PS 7
comments: @daxian-dbw Could you please look the issue?

I see the regression was already in 7.0 Preview1. 
Write-Host works as expected. 
I don't know that is a root of the regression. May be in formatting system. /cc @SteveL-MSFT

This is not in the formatter.  In the formatter, the `MyString` output has `Hidden` as a typename so it's deliberately hidden.  Not sure where that is being set.  In the parser, I can see that only `$Param` has the hidden attribute.  cc @rjmholt
We could try compiled artifacts to find a PR where the regression come but GitHub removes old ones.
This is a regression caused by the `FirstOrDefault` primitive added early in PS7 preview.

:tada:This issue was addressed in #11258, which has now been successfully released as `v7.0.0-rc.1`.:tada:

Handy links:
* [Release Notes](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/releases/tag/v7.0.0-rc.1)

review_comments: If multiple threads access this property, we'll do the work to discover the hidden attribute multiple times. But, I don't believe that would cause a bug, just does needless work. OTOH, the easiest way to make this threadsafe (`Lazy<bool>(IsMemberHidden)`) probably adds some overhead on both generation and access (or we could just add a lock per instance I suppose). So I'm guessing the solution here sells out an uncommon bad case with race conditions (which aren't really race conditions, since the result is always the same) for the usual case?
I see we lock cache tables but not cache elements in the whole file.

To me, this is more of a small optimization so that we don't have to calculate the value every time this property gets accessed. Adding a lock is expensive and not needed in this case given that the operation is so simple that it's OK for multiple threads run in the `if (_isHidden == null)` block occasionally.
Previously, the `ishidden` check happens in higher level like `GetDotNetPropertyImpl` and `GetDotNetMethodImpl`, and it happens every time when those methods called. So having this small optimization is worthwhile.
I agree, just wanted to make sure we discussed it
